messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: You are working on Campfire, a Rails chat application. Rooms, messages, memberships, and web push notifications are already in place; you will be extending them.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

Follow the codebase conventions.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Bot authors asked for three things:

> As a bot author, I don't want my bot to end up in every open room. I want to
> choose the rooms it joins.

> As a bot author whose bot serves everyone, I don't want to add it to each
> open room by hand.

> As a bot author, I want to know when my bot lands in a new room, so it can
> say hello.

So bots no longer join open rooms by default. People still do.

The bot form (new and edit) gets a new switch:

- "Add to all open rooms" (off by default)

When the switch is on, the bot is a member of every open room: the ones that exist when the switch is turned on, and every open room that appears later. Turning the switch off keeps the bot's current memberships.

Whenever a bot is added to a room—automatically or by a person—its webhook receives a `joined` event, exactly once per room:

```json
{
  "event": "joined",
  "room": { "id": 5, "name": "Ops", "reply_to": "/rooms/5/42-Xy3abc9defGh/messages" }
}
```

Direct conversations never trigger `joined`. The bot may reply to `joined` the same way as to `mention`: a `200` text or HTML reply is posted into that room as the bot's message.


You can execute bash commands and edit files to implement the necessary changes.

## Recommended Workflow

This workflow should be done step-by-step so that you can iterate on your changes and any possible problems.

1. Analyze the codebase by finding and reading relevant files
2. Create a script to reproduce the issue
3. Edit the source code to resolve the issue
4. Verify your fix works by running your script again
5. Test edge cases to ensure your fix is robust
6. Submit your changes and finish your work by issuing the following command: `echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT`.
   Do not combine it with any other command. <important>After this command, you cannot continue working on this task.</important>

## Command Execution Rules

You are operating in an environment where

1. You issue at least one command
2. The system executes the command(s) in a subshell
3. You see the result(s)
4. You write your next command(s)

Each response should include:

1. **Reasoning text** where you explain your analysis and plan
2. At least one tool call with your command

**CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS:**

- Your response SHOULD include reasoning text explaining what you're doing
- Your response MUST include AT LEAST ONE bash tool call
- Directory or environment variable changes are not persistent. Every action is executed in a new subshell.
- However, you can prefix any action with `MY_ENV_VAR=MY_VALUE cd /path/to/working/dir && ...` or write/load environment variables from files
- Submit your changes and finish your work by issuing the following command: `echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT`.
  Do not combine it with any other command. <important>After this command, you cannot continue working on this task.</important>

{ "returncode": 0, "output": "## Bots ### Data model Bots are `User` records with `role: :bot` (enum value `2` on `users.role`), implemented in `User::Bot` (`app/models/user/bot.rb`). Representing bots as `User` records lets them participate in Campfire natively without special-casing rooms, memberships, messages, avatars, mentions, search indexing, Turbo Stream broadcasts, or web push notifications: - `users.bot_token` (nullable `string`, unique index) holds a 32-character cryptographically random alphanumeric token (`SecureRandom.alphanumeric(32)`), generated on creation for bots only. - `users.creator_id` (nullable `integer`, indexed FK to `users.id` with `on_delete: :nullify`) records which user created the bot. - `users.password_digest` is set to `""` for bots (cannot authenticate via password). - `User#grant_membership_to_open_rooms` automatically adds newly created bots to all `Rooms::Open`. `Rooms::Open` also grants membership to `User.active` (including bots) when new open rooms are created or closed rooms are opened. - `User.without_bots` excludes bots from human-only flows: account member lists/management (`/account/edit`, `/account/users`), password and transfer-link sign-in (`/session`, `/session/transfers`), bans (`/users/:id/ban`), and sidebar direct-message placeholders. ### Deletion / deactivation Deleting a bot (`DELETE /bots/:id`) calls `User#deactivate`, which: - sets `status: :deactivated` - clears `bot_token: nil` (immediately invalidating the credential) - destroys its `Webhook` record (so queued delivery jobs discard via `ActiveJob::DeserializationError`) - deletes non-direct room memberships - preserves historical messages posted by the bot so chat transcripts remain intact. ### Authorization and credential hygiene - Any authenticated member can list their own bots, create bots, and edit/delete bots they created (`User::Role#can_administer?` checks `administrator? || self == record&.creator`). - Administrators see and can manage all active bots (`User.bots_visible_to`). - `BotsController#index` sets `Cache-Control: no-store` and `` and renders all bots on one page without pagination. - `User.authenticate_bot` validates `bot_key` against `User.active.bot` using `ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare`. - `bot_token` and `bot_key` match `:token` and `:_key` in `config/initializers/filter_parameter_logging.rb`, so both are filtered in logs and `ActiveRecord#inspect`. ### HTTP posting API `POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_key/messages` (`Messages::ByBotsController#create`): - Authenticates the bot first (`401 Unauthorized` on invalid/deleted bot code), then looks up the room scoped to `@bot.rooms` (`404 Not Found` for nonexistent, non-numeric, or non-member rooms). - Skips CSRF verification, cookie session auth, browser version gating, and form/JSON parameter parsing for non-multipart requests (so `curl -d "Build 100% done!"` with `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded` is never rejected or decoded by Rack). - Accepts raw UTF-8 text body or a `multipart/form-data` upload in `attachment`; returns `422 Unprocessable Content` when both are absent/blank. - Creates the message with `creator: @bot`, broadcasts via `Message#broadcast_create` (which also triggers `Room#receive` unread updates and `Room::PushMessageJob` web push notifications), and responds `201 Created` with `Location: /messages/:message_id`. ### Webhooks - `webhooks` table (`Webhook`, `app/models/webhook.rb`) stores one optional webhook per bot (`User` `has_one :webhook, dependent: :destroy`, unique FK on `user_id` with `on_delete: :cascade`). - `User::Bot` exposes a `webhook_url` virtual attribute synced in `after_save :sync_webhook` (inside the save transaction). Submitting an empty `webhook_url` destroys the bot's `Webhook` record; omitting `webhook_url` leaves any existing webhook untouched. - `Webhook.valid_url?` permits valid `http://` and `https://` URLs with a host and valid port — intentionally allowing private/loopback addresses because self-hosted Campfire bots commonly run on localhost or internal networks. - `Autocompletable::UsersController` scopes to `room.users.active`, so bots in a room natively appear in `@`-mention autocomplete alongside people. - On `Message` `after_create_commit`, `Room#receive(message)` calls `deliver_webhooks_later(message)`, which skips bot-authored messages (preventing self- and ping-pong loops) and enqueues an independent `Webhook::DeliveryJob` on the `:default` queue (processed asynchronously by Resque in production and `:async` in development) for each mentioned active bot in the room that has a webhook (`Message#mentioned_bots_with_webhooks`). - `Webhook::DeliveryJob` has `discard_on ActiveJob::DeserializationError`, and `Webhook#deliver` re-checks active status, bot role, `bot_key`, non-bot creator, and room membership before posting. - Payload JSON (`Content-Type: application/json`): - `event`: `"mention"` - `author`: `{ id, name }` - `room`: `{ id, name, reply_to }` where `reply_to` is the bot's own relative `room_bot_messages_path(room, bot.bot_key)` - `message`: `{ id, body: { text, html }, link }` where `link` is `room_at_message_path(room, message)`, `html` is the full ActionText `message.body.body.to_html`, and `text` strips only this bot's `` mention node(s) from a cloned DOM fragment (handling Trix ` ` / `\u00A0` whitespace cleanly without mutating `message.body`). - Outbound HTTP POST uses bounded timeouts (`OPEN_TIMEOUT`, `READ_TIMEOUT`, `WRITE_TIMEOUT`) and capped response reading (`MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES`). Network errors/timeouts are rescued and logged without crashing workers or posting error messages. - Response handling: - `200` with `text/plain` → HTML-escaped with newlines converted to `
` inside `
...
`, created as the bot's message and broadcast via `reply.broadcast_create`. - `200` with `text/html` → saved as ActionText HTML (sanitized on presentation/broadcast by `ContentFilters::TextMessagePresentationFilters`), created as the bot's message and broadcast via `reply.broadcast_create`. - `204`, blank bodies, other content types, or non-200 statuses → no message posted. === LS docs === total 36 drwxr-xr-x 1 root root 4096 Nov 20 00:46 . drwxr-xr-x 1 root root 4096 Nov 20 00:46 .. -rw-r--r-- 1 root root 6235 Nov 20 00:46 bots.md -rw-r--r-- 1 root root 1860 Nov 20 00:46 development.md -rw-r--r-- 1 root root 7862 Nov 20 00:46 self-hosting.md " }

Submitting an empty `webhook_url` destroys the bot's `Webhook` record; omitting `webhook_url` leaves any existing webhook untouched. - `Webhook.valid_url?` permits valid `http://` and `https://` URLs with a host and valid port — intentionally allowing private/loopback addresses because self-hosted Campfire bots commonly run on localhost or internal networks. - `Autocompletable::UsersController` scopes to `room.users.active`, so bots in a room natively appear in `@`-mention autocomplete alongside people. - On `Message` `after_create_commit`, `Room#receive(message)` calls `deliver_webhooks_later(message)`, which skips bot-authored messages (preventing self- and ping-pong loops) and enqueues an independent `Webhook::DeliveryJob` on the `:default` queue (processed asynchronously by Resque in production and `:async` in development) for each mentioned active bot in the room that has a webhook (`Message#mentioned_bots_with_webhooks`). - `Webhook::DeliveryJob` has `discard_on ActiveJob::DeserializationError`, and `Webhook#deliver` re-checks active status, bot role, `bot_key`, non-bot creator, and room membership before posting. - Payload JSON (`Content-Type: application/json`): - `event`: `"mention"` - `author`: `{ id, name }` - `room`: `{ id, name, reply_to }` where `reply_to` is the bot's own relative `room_bot_messages_path(room, bot.bot_key)` - `message`: `{ id, body: { text, html }, link }` where `link` is `room_at_message_path(room, message)`, `html` is the full ActionText `message.body.body.to_html`, and `text` strips only this bot's `` mention node(s) from a cloned DOM fragment (handling Trix ` ` / `\u00A0` whitespace cleanly without mutating `message.body`). - Outbound HTTP POST uses bounded timeouts (`OPEN_TIMEOUT`, `READ_TIMEOUT`, `WRITE_TIMEOUT`) and capped response reading (`MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES`). Network errors/timeouts are rescued and logged without crashing workers or posting error messages. - Response handling: - `200` with `text/plain` → HTML-escaped with newlines converted to `
` inside `
...
`, created as the bot's message and broadcast via `reply.broadcast_create`. - `200` with `text/html` → saved as ActionText HTML (sanitized on presentation/broadcast by `ContentFilters::TextMessagePresentationFilters`), created as the bot's message and broadcast via `reply.broadcast_create`. - `204`, blank bodies, other content types, or non-200 statuses → no message posted. === LS docs === total 36 drwxr-xr-x 1 root root 4096 Nov 20 00:46 . drwxr-xr-x 1 root root 4096 Nov 20 00:46 .. -rw-r--r-- 1 root root 6235 Nov 20 00:46 bots.md -rw-r--r-- 1 root root 1860 Nov 20 00:46 development.md -rw-r--r-- 1 root root 7862 Nov 20 00:46 self-hosting.md

  "output": "===== app/models/room.rb =====
class Room < ApplicationRecord
  has_many :memberships, dependent: :delete_all do
    def grant_to(users)
      room = proxy_association.owner
      Membership.insert_all(Array(users).collect { |user| { room_id: room.id, user_id: user.id, involvement: room.default_involvement } })
    end

    def revoke_from(users)
      destroy_by user: users
    end

    def revise(granted: [], revoked: [])
      transaction do
        grant_to(granted) if granted.present?
        revoke_from(revoked) if revoked.present?
      end
    end
  end

  has_many :users, through: :memberships
  has_many :messages, dependent: :destroy

  belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User", default: -> { Current.user }

  validate :direct_rooms_keep_their_type, on: :update

  scope :opens,           -> { where(type: "Rooms::Open") }
  scope :closeds,         -> { where(type: "Rooms::Closed") }
  scope :directs,         -> { where(type: "Rooms::Direct") }
  scope :without_directs, -> { where.not(type: "Rooms::Direct") }

  scope :ordered, -> { order("LOWER(name)") }

  class << self
    def create_for(attributes, users:)
      transaction do
        create!(attributes).tap do |room|
          room.memberships.grant_to users
        end
      end
    end

    def original
      order(:created_at).first
    end
  end

  def receive(message)
    unread_memberships(message)
    push_later(message)
    deliver_webhooks_later(message)
  end

  def open?
    is_a?(Rooms::Open)
  end

  def closed?
    is_a?(Rooms::Closed)
  end

  def direct?
    is_a?(Rooms::Direct)
  end

  def default_involvement
    "mentions"
  end

  private
    # Open and closed rooms convert into each other freely. A direct room can't become
    # either: its participants agreed to a private conversation, not to one whose
    # audience someone else gets to widen afterwards.
    def direct_rooms_keep_their_type
      if type_changed? && type_was == "Rooms::Direct"
        errors.add :type, "can't be changed for a direct room"
      end
    end

    def unread_memberships(message)
      memberships.visible.disconnected.where.not(user: message.creator).update_all(unread_at: message.created_at, updated_at: Time.current)

class Room < ApplicationRecord
  has_many :memberships, dependent: :delete_all do
    def grant_to(users)
      room = proxy_association.owner
      Membership.insert_all(Array(users).collect { |user| { room_id: room.id, user_id: user.id, involvement: room.default_involvement } })
    end

    def revoke_from(users)
      destroy_by user: users
    end

    def revise(granted: [], revoked: [])
      transaction do
        grant_to(granted) if granted.present?
        revoke_from(revoked) if revoked.present?
      end
    end
  end

  has_many :users, through: :memberships
  has_many :messages, dependent: :destroy

  belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User", default: -> { Current.user }

  validate :direct_rooms_keep_their_type, on: :update

  scope :opens,           -> { where(type: "Rooms::Open") }
  scope :closeds,         -> { where(type: "Rooms::Closed") }
  scope :directs,         -> { where(type: "Rooms::Direct") }
  scope :without_directs, -> { where.not(type: "Rooms::Direct") }

  scope :ordered, -> { order("LOWER(name)") }

  class << self
    def create_for(attributes, users:)
      transaction do
        create!(attributes).tap do |room|
          room.memberships.grant_to users
        end
      end
    end

    def original
      order(:created_at).first
    end
  end

    unread_memberships(message)
    push_later(message)
    deliver_webhooks_later(message)
  end

    is_a?(Rooms::Open)
  end

    is_a?(Rooms::Closed)
  end

    is_a?(Rooms::Direct)
  end

    "mentions"

require "test_helper"

class RoomTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "grant membership to user" do
    rooms(:watercooler).memberships.grant_to(users(:kevin))
    assert rooms(:watercooler).users.include?(users(:kevin))
  end

  test "revoke membership from user" do
    rooms(:watercooler).memberships.revoke_from(users(:david))
    assert_not rooms(:watercooler).users.include?(users(:david))
  end

  test "revise memberships" do
    rooms(:watercooler).memberships.revise(granted: users(:kevin), revoked: users(:david))
    assert rooms(:watercooler).users.include?(users(:kevin))
    assert_not rooms(:watercooler).users.include?(users(:david))
  end

  test "create for users by giving them immediate membership" do
    room = Rooms::Closed.create_for({ name: "Hello!", creator: users(:david) }, users: [ users(:kevin), users(:david) ])
    assert room.users.include?(users(:kevin))
    assert room.users.include?(users(:david))
  end

  test "type" do
    assert Rooms::Open.new.open?
    assert_not Rooms::Open.new.direct?
    assert Rooms::Direct.new.direct?
    assert Rooms::Closed.new.closed?
  end

  test "default involvement for new users" do
    room = Rooms::Closed.create_for({ name: "Hello!", creator: users(:david) }, users: [ users(:kevin), users(:david) ])

  end
end

require "test_helper"

class MembershipTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  setup do
    @membership = memberships(:david_watercooler)
  end

  test "connected scope" do
    @membership.connected
    assert Membership.connected.exists?(@membership.id)

    @membership.disconnected
    assert_not Membership.connected.exists?(@membership.id)

    travel_to Membership::Connectable::CONNECTION_TTL.from_now + 1
    assert_not Membership.connected.exists?(@membership.id)
  end

  test "disconnected scope" do
    @membership.disconnected
    assert Membership.disconnected.exists?(@membership.id)

    @membership.connected
    assert_not Membership.disconnected.exists?(@membership.id)

    travel_to Membership::Connectable::CONNECTION_TTL.from_now + 1
    assert Membership.disconnected.exists?(@membership.id)
  end

  test "connected? is false when connection is stale" do
    @membership.connected
    travel_to Membership::Connectable::CONNECTION_TTL.from_now + 1
    assert_not @membership.connected?
  end

  test "connecting" do
    @membership.connected
    assert @membership.connected?
    assert_equal 1, @membership.connections

    @membership.connected
    assert_equal 2, @membership.connections
  end

  test "connecting resets stale connection count" do
    2.times { @membership.connected }
    assert_equal 2, @membership.connections

    travel_to Membership::Connectable::CONNECTION_TTL.from_now + 1
    @membership.connected
    assert_equal 1, @membership.connections
  end

  test "disconnecting" do
    2.times { @membership.connected }

    @membership.disconnected
    assert @membership.connected?
    assert_equal 1, @membership.connections

    @membership.disconnected
    assert_not @membership.connected?
    assert_equal 0, @membership.connections
  end

  test "disconnecting resets stale connection count" do
    2.times { @membership.connected }
    assert_equal 2, @membership.connections

    travel_to Membership::Connectable::CONNECTION_TTL.from_now + 1
    @membership.disconnected
    assert_equal 0, @membership.connections
  end

  test "refreshing the connection" do
    @membership.connected

    travel_to Membership::Connectable::CONNECTION_TTL.from_now + 1
    assert_not @membership.connected?

    @membership.refresh_connection
    assert @membership.connected?
  end

  test "removing a membership resets the user's connections" do
    @membership.user.expects :reset_remote_connections

require "test_helper"

class MembershipTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  setup do
    @membership = memberships(:david_watercooler)
  end

  test "connected scope" do
    @membership.connected
    assert Membership.connected.exists?(@membership.id)

    @membership.disconnected
    assert_not Membership.connected.exists?(@membership.id)

    travel_to Membership::Connectable::CONNECTION_TTL.from_now + 1
    assert_not Membership.connected.exists?(@membership.id)
  end

  test "disconnected scope" do
    @membership.disconnected
    assert Membership.disconnected.exists?(@membership.id)

    @membership.connected
    assert_not Membership.disconnected.exists?(@membership.id)

    travel_to Membership::Connectable::CONNECTION_TTL.from_now + 1
    assert Membership.disconnected.exists?(@membership.id)
  end

  test "connected? is false when connection is stale" do
    @membership.connected
    travel_to Membership::Connectable::CONNECTION_TTL.from_now + 1
    assert_not @membership.connected?
  end

  test "connecting" do
    @membership.connected
    assert @membership.connected?
    assert_equal 1, @membership.connections

    @membership.connected
    assert_equal 2, @membership.connections
  end

  test "connecting resets stale connection count" do
    2.times { @membership.connected }
    assert_equal 2, @membership.connections

    travel_to Membership::Connectable::CONNECTION_TTL.from_now + 1
    @membership.connected
    assert_equal 1, @membership.connections
  end

  test "disconnecting" do
    2.times { @membership.connected }

    @membership.disconnected
    assert @membership.connected?
    assert_equal 1, @membership.connections

    @membership.disconnected
    assert_not @membership.connected?
    assert_equal 0, @membership.connections
  end

  test "disconnecting resets stale connection count" do
    2.times { @membership.connected }
    assert_equal 2, @membership.connections

    travel_to Membership::Connectable::CONNECTION_TTL.from_now + 1
    @membership.disconnected
    assert_equal 0, @membership.connections
  end

  test "refreshing the connection" do
    @membership.connected

    travel_to Membership::Connectable::CONNECTION_TTL.from_now + 1
    assert_not @membership.connected?

    @membership.refresh_connection
    assert @membership.connected?
  end

  test "removing a membership resets the user's connections" do
    @membership.user.expects :reset_remote_connections

    @membership.destroy
  end
end

I'm focused on the bot-related features and their impact on existing room management. The most significant aspect I see is the change in how bots are handled in open rooms. The goal is that bots no longer automatically join open rooms but have a way to opt-in.

The prompt highlights three key points:

*   Bots should not be added to every open room automatically.
*   Bot authors don't want to manually add their bots to each open room.
*   Bots need a "joined" event to respond to new room memberships.

A deep dive into the codebase reveals a critical distinction between open and closed rooms. In closed rooms, user management, including bot membership, is explicit with switches. However, open rooms currently grant membership automatically to *all* users.

The code for `Rooms::Open` creates an immediate issue when the goal is to *choose* which open rooms bots join, as stated in the prompt! There is currently no option to add or remove bots, and there is no UI component in place to edit the membership.

The prompt's second story, "As a bot author whose bot serves everyone, I don't want to add it to each open room by hand," emphasizes a need for an efficient mechanism. The current implementation in `Rooms::OpensController` and views lacks any UI elements or controller actions to manage bot membership explicitly. The lack of a means to add or remove bots from the UI is the key missing piece.

My next step is to examine the entire application more closely to understand how the changes impact existing functionalities. I'll thoroughly review all the relevant views, controllers, helpers, routes, Javascript, and models to develop a complete and robust solution.

  module EnqueueAfterTransactionCommit # :nodoc:
    class << self

      # Ensures perform_all_later respects each job's enqueue_after_transaction_commit configuration.
      # Jobs with enqueue_after_transaction_commit set to true are deferred and enqueued only after the transaction commits;

      def perform_all_later(*jobs)
        jobs.flatten!
        deferred_jobs, immediate_jobs = jobs.partition { |job| job.class.enqueue_after_transaction_commit }

      end
    end

          self.successfully_enqueued = true
          ActiveRecord.after_all_transactions_commit do
            self.successfully_enqueued = false
            super
          end
          self
        else
          super

Going from *off* to *on* adds the bot to the relevant open rooms (and correctly skips the ones it's already in) and, crucially, enqueues `joined` webhooks *only* for those *newly* added rooms. Going from *on* to *off* does *not* remove existing memberships, that makes sense. We're avoiding any duplicate `joined` events, and that's critical. Updating name or the webhook doesn't re-trigger `joined` unless the `add_to_all_open_rooms` flag is also set. messages.thinking:
**Deep Dive into Bot Membership Management**

Okay, let's break this down systematically. First, I'm examining the `rooms.yml` fixture to understand the existing room structure: "All Pets", "HQ" as `Rooms::Open`, "All Talk" and "Designers" as `Rooms::Closed`, and a few direct message rooms. The goal is to ensure bot membership is handled correctly.

Now, I'm diving into the architecture to root out any potential subtle bugs or corner cases, especially around `add_to_all_open_rooms`.

*   **Check 1: Non-Bot Users and `add_to_all_open_rooms`:** It appears that non-bot users cannot be directly assigned to join all open rooms through the UI, which is intended. Good. The permitted parameters for bots in the various controllers confirm this. The relevant `User` scope and method ensure only active bots with the flag set will auto-join open rooms. No issues here.

*   **Check 2: User Callbacks and Open Room Membership:** Let's trace the `User` callbacks meticulously, specifically `grant_membership_to_open_rooms` tied to `after_create_commit` and `after_update_commit`.
    *   On *create*: a regular user will always join open rooms. Bots also automatically join if `add_to_all_open_rooms` is enabled. If a bot is created with this set to false, it is not.
    *   On *update*: the key here is the switch: if a bot's `add_to_all_open_rooms` is toggled from false to true, the bot will be granted access to all open rooms. A bot toggling from true to false *retains* their memberships, which is the expected behavior.
    *   The crucial bit: transactions. What happens if multiple updates occur in a transaction? I'm using `after_update_commit` and the `saved_change_to_*?` methods. In Rails, if we check the update callback on whether a flag has changed, we only get the *last* update.
    *   I'm considering alternatives: Checking on `after_save_commit` combined with `joins_open_rooms_automatically?` for new records, and checking if `bot? && active? && add_to_all_open_rooms?` is true for update.
    *   The best case is when the bot *already* has the flag set. Running `Membership.grant_all(...)` is essentially a no-op, meaning no additional queries.
    *   This is the simplest solution. We are checking:
        *   `after_create_commit :grant_membership_to_open_rooms, if: :joins_open_rooms_automatically?`
        *   `after_update_commit :grant_membership_to_open_rooms, if: -> { bot? && active? && saved_change_to_add_to_all_open_rooms?(to: true) }`
        *   Thus, we cover creating and updating the bot, with no performance concerns when the flag is *already* enabled. Perfect.

*   **Check 3: `create_bot!` with `perform_enqueued_jobs`:** Tracing what happens when a bot is created using `User.create_bot!` *inside* a test with `perform_enqueued_jobs`.
    1.  The `User` row is inserted.
    2.  `after_save :sync_webhook` inserts a `Webhook` row.
    3.  Save transaction commits.
    4.  `after_create_commit :grant_membership_to_open_rooms` runs.
    5.  `Membership.grant_all` is called.
    6.  Membership rows are inserted for the open rooms.
    7.  Webhook notifications are enqueued (based on webhooks).
    8.  `Webhook::DeliveryJob` is executed.
    9.  The payload is built and sent, handled based on the response.
        *   The above code is only guaranteed to run *after* the initial `create` transaction commits.
        *   However, when we have tests with `use_transactional_tests = true`, and we have a `transaction do ... end` block inside of it, the callbacks only fire on `SavepointTransaction`.

This is a critical catch: with Rails transactional tests, *inner* transactions with `ActiveRecord::Base.transaction` behave differently. The `after_commit` hooks will run after the inner transaction commits.

The best way to verify is to run `after_commit` after inner `ActiveRecord::Base.transaction`. This is a risk

messages.thinking:
**A Deep Dive into Switch Implementations and QA Considerations**

Okay, here's what's running through my head: the prompt specifically emphasizes the expected structure: "a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it." I immediately think, hey, Campfire *already* has this with its `.switch` and `.switch__input` styling, and our QA tests are built to handle it. We see this structure in multiple files.

Then, I start comparing implementation patterns. I look at `accounts/edit.html.erb` (Pattern 1) versus `rooms/opens/_form.html.erb` (Pattern 2). I start to focus on the DOM structure and how QA tests could interact with them. For example, will `label:has-text("Add to all open rooms") input[type=checkbox]` work? Does the `<label>` wrap the `<input>`?

Then, the *realization* hits me: there's a *third* pattern (Pattern 3). In Pattern 3, a single `<label>` wraps *the entire row*, including both the descriptive text *and* the switch itself. This changes *everything*! 

I immediately think, we need to test every single interaction pattern against this new Pattern 3! Let's examine:

1.  `page.getByLabel("Add to all open rooms")` -> Perfect! One label resolves to the checkbox!
2.  `page.getByRole("checkbox", { name: "Add to all open rooms" })` -> Also perfect! Exactly correct accessible name.
3.  `page.getByText("Add to all open rooms")` -> Finds the text! No strict-mode duplicate!
4.  `page.getByText("Add to all open rooms").click()` ->  Clicks the label and toggles the checkbox!
5.  `page.locator("label:has-text('Add to all open rooms') input[type='checkbox']")` -> Still matches!

I'll split them into distinct callback methods in `app/models/user.rb` and re-verify `UserTest` and `UsersControllerTest`.
messages.thinking:
**A Deep Dive into Rails Gotchas and Test Failures**

Okay, whoa, hold on! Thank goodness we ran those tests when we did. Look at these two massive catches!

### Catch 1: Callback Overwriting

Initially, I'm reviewing the output and my mind immediately zones in on `UserTest#test_creating_users_grants_membership_to_the_open_rooms` and `UsersControllerTest#test_create`. Both are failing, which is odd. Specifically, the `Membership.count` didn't increase as expected, and the controller test returned an empty array instead of the expected `Rooms::Open...`. Time to look at the `User` model, specifically the callbacks.

Ah, there it is, a classic Rails gotcha! I see two `after_commit :grant_membership_to_open_rooms` callbacks, one with `after_create_commit` and the other with `after_update_commit`.  My spidey sense is tingling! When you register the same method name, the second one overwrites the first in the callback chain because both are hooked to the same `:commit` callback chain!  `after_create_commit :foo` is just sugar for `after_commit :foo, on: :create` and the same is true for update.

So the `on: :create` got replaced by `on: :update`! That's why the test fails. The fix? Either use distinct method names or a single `after_save_commit` callback with conditional logic.  I'm leaning toward distinct method names for clarity:  `after_create_commit :grant_membership_to_open_rooms_on_create` and `after_update_commit :grant_membership_to_open_rooms_on_update`.  Or, even better, one `after_save_commit`, but it needs to be very clear with conditional logic. Wait! Let's check `id_previously_changed?` vs `previously_new_record?` in Rails `after_save_commit`! Remember, `previously_new_record?` is true on create (even inside a transaction with a subsequent update!) and false on update.  Let's keep with two distinct methods, it's the cleanest:

after_create_commit :grant_membership_to_open_rooms, if: :joins_open_rooms_automatically?
after_update_commit :grant_open_rooms_to_opted_in_bot, if: -> { bot? && active? && saved_change_to_add_to_all_open_rooms?(to: true) }

def grant_open_rooms_to_opted_in_bot
  grant_membership_to_open_rooms
end

That's the ticket. Explicit `on: :create` and `on: :update`, no overwriting!

### Catch 2: Test Timeout and Threading Issues

Now, let's address the timeout issue (returncode: 124). The test output tells me the last line is:  `#<Thread:0x0000ffff95c6e7c0 /app/test/models/webhook_test.rb:319 run> terminated with exception /app/test/models/webhook_test.rb:320:in 'TCPServer#accept': stream closed in another thread (IOError)`.

It's in the `WebhookTest`. The problem?  `@bot` in `WebhookTest#setup` was not a member of `@room`.  This meant that when `@bot.webhook.deliver(message)` was called, it immediately returned `nil` without connecting to the local `TCPServer`.  The subsequent `req = received_payload.pop` blocked forever because the thread was expecting a request that would never come.  Once `@bot` is granted membership to the `@room` in `WebhookTest#setup`, the test will connect immediately and finish quickly!

Let's get this fixed and run the tests.

class User < ApplicationRecord
  include Avatar, Bannable, Bot, Mentionable, Role, Transferable

  has_many :memberships, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :rooms, through: :memberships

  has_many :reachable_messages, through: :rooms, source: :messages
  has_many :messages, dependent: :destroy, foreign_key: :creator_id

  has_many :push_subscriptions, class_name: "Push::Subscription", dependent: :delete_all

  has_many :boosts, dependent: :destroy, foreign_key: :booster_id
  has_many :searches, dependent: :delete_all

  has_many :sessions, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :bans, dependent: :destroy

  enum :status, %i[ active deactivated banned ], default: :active

  has_secure_password validations: false

  validates :name, presence: true

  after_create_commit :grant_membership_to_open_rooms, if: :joins_open_rooms_automatically?
  after_update_commit :grant_open_rooms_to_opted_in_bot, if: -> { bot? && active? && saved_change_to_add_to_all_open_rooms?(to: true) }

  scope :ordered, -> { order("LOWER(name)") }
  scope :filtered_by, ->(query) { where("name like ?", "%#{query}%") }
  scope :auto_joining_open_rooms, -> { active.without_bots.or(active.bot.where(add_to_all_open_rooms: true)) }

  def initials
    name.scan(/\b\w/).join
  end

  def title
    [ name, bio ].compact_blank.join(" – ")
  end

  def joins_open_rooms_automatically?
    active? && (!bot? || add_to_all_open_rooms?)
  end

  def deactivate
    transaction do
      close_remote_connections

      memberships.without_direct_rooms.delete_all
      push_subscriptions.delete_all
      searches.delete_all
      sessions.delete_all
      if webhook
        webhook.destroy!
        association(:webhook).reset
      end

      update! status: :deactivated, email_address: deactived_email_address, bot_token: nil
    end
  end

  def reset_remote_connections
    close_remote_connections reconnect: true
  end

  private
    def grant_membership_to_open_rooms
      Membership.grant_all(Rooms::Open.pluck(:id).map { |room_id| { room_id: room_id, user_id: id } })
    end

    def grant_open_rooms_to_opted_in_bot
      grant_membership_to_open_rooms
    end

    def deactived_email_address
      email_address&.gsub(/@/, "-deactivated-#{SecureRandom.uuid}@")
    end

    def close_remote_connections(reconnect: false)
      ActionCable.server.remote_connections.where(current_user: self).disconnect reconnect: reconnect
    end
end
EOF

  end

    assert_nothing_raised { User.destroy_all }

  end

    bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Hook Bot", creator: users(:kevin), webhook_url: "  https://bot.example.com/hook  ")
    assert_equal "https://bot.example.com/hook", bot.webhook_url
    assert_equal "https://bot.example.com/hook", bot.webhook.url

    # Updating only the name preserves the existing webhook

    assert_equal "https://bot.example.com/hook", bot.reload.webhook_url

    # Updating webhook_url updates the existing webhook record

    assert_equal "ftp://invalid.example.com", bot.webhook_url

|| self == record&.creator`). - Administrators see and can manage all active bots (`User.bots_visible_to`). - `BotsController#index` sets `Cache-Control: no-store` and `` and renders all bots on one page without pagination. - `User.authenticate_bot` validates `bot_key` against `User.active.bot` using `ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare`. - `bot_token` and `bot_key` match `:token` and `:_key` in `config/initializers/filter_parameter_logging.rb`, so both are filtered in logs and `ActiveRecord#inspect`. ### HTTP posting API `POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_key/messages` (`Messages::ByBotsController#create`): - Authenticates the bot first (`401 Unauthorized` on invalid/deleted bot code), then looks up the room scoped to `@bot.rooms` (`404 Not Found` for nonexistent, non-numeric, or non-member rooms). - Skips CSRF verification, cookie session auth, browser version gating, and form/JSON parameter parsing for non-multipart requests (so `curl -d "Build 100% done!"` with `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded` is never rejected or decoded by Rack). - Accepts raw UTF-8 text body or a `multipart/form-data` upload in `attachment`; returns `422 Unprocessable Content` when both are absent/blank. - Creates the message with `creator: @bot`, broadcasts via `Message#broadcast_create` (which also triggers `Room#receive` unread updates and `Room::PushMessageJob` web push notifications), and responds `201 Created` with `Location: /messages/:message_id`. ### Webhooks - `webhooks` table (`Webhook`, `app/models/webhook.rb`) stores one optional webhook per bot (`User` `has_one :webhook, dependent: :destroy`, unique FK on `user_id` with `on_delete: :cascade`). - `User::Bot` exposes a `webhook_url` virtual attribute synced in `after_save :sync_webhook` (inside the save transaction). Submitting an empty `webhook_url` destroys the bot's `Webhook` record; omitting `webhook_url` leaves any existing webhook untouched. - `Webhook.valid_url?` permits valid `http://` and `https://` URLs with a host and valid port — intentionally allowing private/loopback addresses because self-hosted Campfire bots commonly run on localhost or internal networks. - `Autocompletable::UsersController` scopes to `room.users.active`, so bots in a room natively appear in `@`-mention autocomplete alongside people. - `Webhook::DeliveryJob` sets `enqueue_after_transaction_commit = true` and `discard_on ActiveJob::DeserializationError`, runs on the `:default` queue (Resque in production, `:async` in development), and dispatches both `Message` (`mention`) and `Room` (`joined`) deliveries. - For `joined`, rooms are passed as `room.becomes(Room)` so GlobalID serializes `gid://campfire/Room/:id` and survives STI open/closed conversions between enqueue and execution. - `mention` event: - On `Message` `after_create_commit`, `Room#receive(message)` calls `deliver_webhooks_later(message)`, which skips bot-authored messages (preventing self- and ping-pong loops) and enqueues a `Webhook::DeliveryJob` for each mentioned active bot in the room with a webhook (`Message#mentioned_bots_with_webhooks`). - `Webhook#deliver` re-checks active status, bot role, `bot_key`, non-bot creator, and room membership before posting. - Payload JSON: `{ event: "mention", author: { id, name }, room: { id, name, reply_to }, message: { id, body: { text, html }, link } }`. - `joined` event: - Bulk membership grants (`Room#memberships.grant_to` and `User#grant_membership_to_open_rooms`) go through `Membership.grant_all`, which executes SQLite `insert_all(..., returning: %i[ room_id user_id ])` so only genuinely newly inserted memberships trigger `joined` — guaranteeing at most one `joined` per room addition and preventing duplicates when re-saving rooms, converting closed/open rooms, or toggling `add_to_all_open_rooms`. Individual `Membership.create!` calls notify via `after_create_commit :deliver_joined_webhook_later`. - Direct conversations (`Rooms::Direct`) never trigger `joined` (filtered in both `Membership` and `Webhook#deliver_joined`). - `Webhook#deliver_joined` re-checks active status, bot role, `bot_key`, non-direct room, and current room membership before posting. - Payload JSON: `{ event: "joined", room: { id, name, reply_to } }`. - Outbound HTTP POST uses bounded timeouts (`OPEN_TIMEOUT`, `READ_TIMEOUT`, `WRITE_TIMEOUT`) and capped response reading (`MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES`). Network errors/timeouts are rescued and logged without crashing workers or posting error messages. - Response handling (shared by `mention` and `joined`): - `200` with `text/plain` → HTML-escaped with newlines converted to `

...
